title: Reasons for Scrapping Off-peak Monthly Travel Pass for Persons with Disabilities and Senior Citizens
what_it_is: Reasons for Scrapping Off-peak Monthly Travel Pass for Persons with Disabilities and Senior Citizens

sections.label: Off-peak pass discontinued, new discount
sections.summary: The off-peak pass, introduced in July 2015, shifted fewer than 200 users, so the PTC recommended discontinuing it for a new scheme giving up to 50 cents discount for taps in before 7.45 am.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: The off-peak pass was introduced in July 2015 as a trial to see if we can get regular commuters to shift from peak to off-peak travel.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: It has shifted less than 200 of the pass users to off-peak travel.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: As the scheme has clearly not been effective, the Public Transport Council (PTC) recommended discontinuing it starting this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Instead, under a new scheme, all commuters can enjoy a fare discount of up to 50 cents throughout the rail network if they tap in before 7.45 am.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Senior citizens and persons with disabilities enjoy this discount on top of their regular 25% discounts.

sections.label: Seniors switch to monthly concession pass
sections.summary: Over half of senior and disabled off-peak pass users switched to the monthly concession pass in January, and the Minister says disbanding the scheme is right as the new scheme benefits many commuters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: More than half of the senior citizens and persons with disabilities off-peak pass users have switched to buy the monthly concession pass in January this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Minister, can you also clarify whether you are taking both Question Nos 13 and 14 together?

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: I do not have the data that Er Dr Lee Bee Wah has asked for, except to say that when we design a public scheme, it must benefit as wide a number of people as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Unfortunately, it did not turn out to be so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: I think it is the right decision on the part of PTC to recommend disbanding this but, instead, bring out a new scheme, which is what we are enjoying today, which will benefit hundreds and thousands of commuters.
